1	﻿function Test-MtCisManagedDeviceForAuthentication {
     2	    <#
     3	    .SYNOPSIS
     4	        Checks that a Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device for all users and apps.
     5	
     6	    .DESCRIPTION
     7	        Checks that at least one enabled Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device for all users in all cloud apps. A hybrid joined device may optionally be allowed as an alternative with the OR operator.
     8	        CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 (5.2.2.9, L1)
     9	
    10	    .EXAMPLE
    11	        Test-MtCisManagedDeviceForAuthentication
    12	
    13	        Returns true if an enabled policy requires a compliant device for all users and all cloud apps, optionally allowing a hybrid joined device.
    14	
    15	    .LINK
    16	        https://maester.dev/docs/tests/CIS.M365.5.2.2.9
    17	    #>
    18	    [MaesterTest(
    19	        Id = 'CIS.M365.5.2.2.9',
    20	        Title = 'Ensure a managed device is required for authentication',
    21	        Product = 'entra',
    22	        Feature = 'conditional-access',
    23	        Area = 'access-control',
    24	        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
    25	        Severity = 'Medium',
    26	        UserImpact = 'High',
    27	        ImplementationCost = 'High',
    28	        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
    29	        Control = ('cis-m365:5.2.2.9', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-3'),
    30	        Service = 'Graph',
    31	        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
    32	        Author = 'JeremyFinney-lgtm'
    33	    )]
    34	    [CmdletBinding()]
    35	    [OutputType([bool])]
    36	    param()
    37	
    38	    Write-Verbose 'Getting Conditional Access policies...'
    39	    $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy
    40	
    41	    $candidates = @($policies | Where-Object { @($_.grantControls.builtInControls) -contains 'compliantDevice' -or @($_.grantControls.builtInControls) -contains 'domainJoinedDevice' })
    42	
    43	    $report = foreach ($policy in $candidates) {
    44	        $grants = @($policy.grantControls.builtInControls)
    45	        $otherGrants = @($grants | Where-Object { $_ -ne 'compliantDevice' -and $_ -ne 'domainJoinedDevice' })
    46	        $problems = @(Get-MtCisConditionalAccessScopeProblem -Policy $policy -Users AllUsers)
    47	        $checks = [ordered]@{
    48	            'Scope covers the required users and apps' = $problems.Count -eq 0
    49	            'Compliant device required' = $grants -contains 'compliantDevice' -and $otherGrants.Count -eq 0
    50	            'Operator is OR' = $policy.grantControls.operator -eq 'OR'
    51	            'Enabled' = $policy.state -eq 'enabled'
    52	        }
    53	        $failed = @($checks.GetEnumerator() | Where-Object { -not $_.Value } | ForEach-Object { $_.Key })
    54	        $failedText = $failed -join ', '
    55	        if ($problems.Count -gt 0) { $failedText += " ($($problems -join '; '))" }
    56	        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $policy.displayName; State = $policy.state; Failed = $failedText; Pass = $failed.Count -eq 0 }
    57	    }
    58	    $testResult = @($report | Where-Object { $_.Pass }).Count -gt 0
    59	    $passText = 'An enabled Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device for all users and all cloud apps, optionally allowing a hybrid joined device.'
    60	    $failText = if ($candidates.Count -eq 0) { 'No Conditional Access policy that requires a compliant or hybrid joined device was found.' } else { 'No enabled Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device for all users and all cloud apps.' }
    61	
    62	    $resultMd = "| Policy | State | Failed checks | Result |`n"
    63	    $resultMd += "| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
    64	    foreach ($row in $report) {
    65	        $resultMd += "| $($row.Name) | $($row.State) | $(if ($row.Failed) { $row.Failed } else { 'None' }) | $(if ($row.Pass) { '✅ Pass' } else { '❌ Fail' }) |`n"
    66	    }
    67	
    68	    if ($testResult) {
    69	        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. $passText`n`n%TestResult%"
    70	    } else {
    71	        $testResultMarkdown = "$failText`n`n%TestResult%"
    72	    }
    73	    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace '%TestResult%', $resultMd
    74	
    75	    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    76	    return $testResult
    77	}

content.content:
﻿An enabled Conditional Access policy requires a compliant device for all users and all cloud apps. A hybrid-joined device may optionally be allowed as an alternative.

A stolen password or session token is far less useful when sign-in is limited to devices that your organisation manages and that meet its security baseline. Unmanaged devices are the usual source of malware that steals tokens.

This is a high-impact control: personal and partner devices lose access unless you provide an alternative such as browser-only access with session controls. Enrol devices in Microsoft Intune and define compliance policies before enabling the policy, and use report-only mode first.

User and group exclusions are not evaluated by this test. Application exclusions are also not evaluated when the policy targets all apps; verify exclusions are documented and reviewed annually. A condition that narrows the policy is reported unless the check is about that condition.

#### Remediation action

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com).
2. Go to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > [**Policies**](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies) and select **New policy**.
3. Under **Users**, include **All users**. Exclude your emergency access accounts.
4. Under **Target resources**, select **All resources (formerly All cloud apps)**.
5. Under **Grant**, select **Grant access**, then **Require device to be marked as compliant** and optionally **Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device**. Choose **Require one of the selected controls**.
6. Set **Enable policy** to **On** (use **Report-only** first to measure the impact) and select **Create**.

#### Related links

* [Microsoft Entra admin center - Conditional Access policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies)
* [Require compliant or hybrid joined devices with Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/conditional-access/policy-all-users-device-compliance)
* [Require a compliant device in Conditional Access](https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/intune-service/protect/create-conditional-access-intune)
* [CIS Microsoft 365 Foundations Benchmark v7.0.0 - 5.2.2.9](https://www.cisecurity.org/benchmark/microsoft_365)

     1	﻿function Get-MtCisConditionalAccessScopeProblem {
     2	    <#
     3	    .SYNOPSIS
     4	        Returns why a Conditional Access policy does not cover the users and applications that a CIS check requires.
     5	
     6	    .DESCRIPTION
     7	        Reads who the policy includes, which applications it targets and which conditions narrow it. User and group
     8	        exclusions, and application exclusions for all-app policies, are not evaluated. A narrowing condition is
     9	        reported unless the check is about that condition.
    10	
    11	    .PARAMETER Policy
    12	        A Conditional Access policy as returned by Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy.
    13	
    14	    .PARAMETER Users
    15	        AllUsers requires All in includeUsers. AdministratorRoles also accepts a policy that includes every role from Get-MtCisAdministratorRole.
    16	
    17	    .PARAMETER Applications
    18	        All, or the application IDs or user action that the check targets.
    19	
    20	    .PARAMETER TargetedCondition
    21	        Narrowing conditions that the check itself is about. These are not reported.
    22	
    23	    .EXAMPLE
    24	        Get-MtCisConditionalAccessScopeProblem -Policy $policy -Users AllUsers
    25	
    26	        Returns reasons when the policy does not cover all users and all cloud apps.
    27	
    28	    .OUTPUTS
    29	        System.String
    30	    #>
    31	    [CmdletBinding()]
    32	    [OutputType([string[]])]
    33	    param(
    34	        [Parameter(Mandatory)]
    35	        [object] $Policy,
    36	
    37	        [ValidateSet('AllUsers', 'AdministratorRoles', 'NotNone')]
    38	        [string] $Users = 'AllUsers',
    39	
    40	        [string[]] $Applications = @('All'),
    41	
    42	        [ValidateSet('Platforms', 'Locations', 'DeviceFilter', 'ClientAppTypes', 'UserRiskLevels', 'SignInRiskLevels', 'InsiderRiskLevels', 'AuthenticationFlows')]
    43	        [string[]] $TargetedCondition = @()
    44	    )
    45	
    46	    # The two roles that Test-MtCaExclusionForDirectorySyncAccount expects a policy to exclude.
    47	    $syncRoleIds = @('d29b2b05-8046-44ba-8758-1e26182fcf32', 'a92aed5d-d78a-4d16-b381-09adb37eb3b0')
    48	    $problems = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
    49	    $conditions = $Policy.conditions
    50	    $userScope = $conditions.users
    51	    $appScope = $conditions.applications
    52	
    53	    $includedUsers = @($userScope.includeUsers | Where-Object { $_ })
    54	    if ($Users -eq 'AllUsers') {
    55	        if ($includedUsers -notcontains 'All') { $problems.Add('not all users are included') }
    56	    } elseif ($Users -eq 'AdministratorRoles') {
    57	        $includedRoles = @($userScope.includeRoles | Where-Object { $_ })
    58	        $missingRoles = @(Get-MtCisAdministratorRole | Where-Object { $includedRoles -notcontains $_.Id } | ForEach-Object { $_.Name })
    59	        if ($missingRoles.Count -gt 0) { $problems.Add("administrative roles not included: $($missingRoles -join ', ')") }
    60	    } elseif ($includedUsers.Count -eq 0 -or $includedUsers -contains 'None') {
    61	        $problems.Add('no users are included')
    62	    }
    63	    foreach ($id in @($userScope.excludeRoles | Where-Object { $_ })) {
    64	        if ($syncRoleIds -notcontains $id) { $problems.Add("excludes role $id") }
    65	    }
    66	
    67	    $includedApps = @($appScope.includeApplications | Where-Object { $_ })
    68	    $includedActions = @($appScope.includeUserActions | Where-Object { $_ })
    69	    $excludedApps = @($appScope.excludeApplications | Where-Object { $_ })
    70	    if ($Applications -contains 'All') {
    71	        if ($includedApps -notcontains 'All') { $problems.Add('not all cloud apps are included') }
    72	    } else {
    73	        $covered = @($includedApps + $includedActions)
    74	        $notTargeted = @($Applications | Where-Object { $covered -notcontains $_ })
    75	        if ($notTargeted.Count -gt 0) { $problems.Add("does not target $($notTargeted -join ', ')") }
    76	        $targetExcluded = @($Applications | Where-Object { $excludedApps -contains $_ })
    77	        if ($targetExcluded.Count -gt 0) { $problems.Add("excludes $($targetExcluded -join ', ')") }
    78	    }
    79	
    80	    if ('Platforms' -notin $TargetedCondition -and $conditions.platforms) {
    81	        $includedPlatforms = @($conditions.platforms.includePlatforms | Where-Object { $_ })
    82	        $excludedPlatforms = @($conditions.platforms.excludePlatforms | Where-Object { $_ })
    83	        if (($includedPlatforms.Count -gt 0 -and $includedPlatforms -notcontains 'all') -or $excludedPlatforms.Count -gt 0) {
    84	            $problems.Add('platforms are limited')
    85	        }
    86	    }
    87	    if ('Locations' -notin $TargetedCondition -and $conditions.locations) {
    88	        $includedLocations = @($conditions.locations.includeLocations | Where-Object { $_ })
    89	        $excludedLocations = @($conditions.locations.excludeLocations | Where-Object { $_ })
    90	        if (($includedLocations.Count -gt 0 -and $includedLocations -notcontains 'All') -or $excludedLocations.Count -gt 0) {
    91	            $problems.Add('locations are limited')
    92	        }
    93	    }
    94	    if ('DeviceFilter' -notin $TargetedCondition -and $conditions.devices.deviceFilter.rule) {
    95	        $problems.Add('a device filter applies')
    96	    }
    97	    if ('ClientAppTypes' -notin $TargetedCondition) {
    98	        $clientAppTypes = @($conditions.clientAppTypes | Where-Object { $_ })
    99	        if ($clientAppTypes.Count -gt 0 -and $clientAppTypes -notcontains 'all') { $problems.Add('client app types are limited') }
   100	    }
   101	    if ('UserRiskLevels' -notin $TargetedCondition -and @($conditions.userRiskLevels | Where-Object { $_ }).Count -gt 0) {
   102	        $problems.Add('a user risk condition is set')
   103	    }
   104	    if ('SignInRiskLevels' -notin $TargetedCondition -and @($conditions.signInRiskLevels | Where-Object { $_ }).Count -gt 0) {
   105	        $problems.Add('a sign-in risk condition is set')
   106	    }
   107	    if ('InsiderRiskLevels' -notin $TargetedCondition -and @($conditions.insiderRiskLevels | Where-Object { $_ }).Count -gt 0) {
   108	        $problems.Add('an insider risk condition is set')
   109	    }
   110	    if ('AuthenticationFlows' -notin $TargetedCondition -and @($conditions.authenticationFlows.transferMethods | Where-Object { $_ }).Count -gt 0) {
   111	        $problems.Add('authentication flows are limited')
   112	    }
   113	
   114	    return [string[]]$problems.ToArray()
   115	}

1	﻿function Test-MtCisaManagedDevice {
     2	    <#
     3	    .SYNOPSIS
     4	    Checks if a Conditional Access policy requiring managed device is enabled
     5	
     6	    .DESCRIPTION
     7	    Managed devices SHOULD be required for authentication.
     8	
     9	    .EXAMPLE
    10	    Test-MtCisaManagedDevice
    11	
    12	    Returns true if at least one policy requires managed devices
    13	
    14	    .LINK
    15	    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtCisaManagedDevice
    16	    #>
    17	    [MaesterTest(
    18	        Id = 'CISA.MS.AAD.3.7',
    19	        Title = 'Managed devices SHOULD be required for authentication.',
    20	        Product = 'entra',
    21	        Feature = 'conditional-access',
    22	        Area = 'access-control',
    23	        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
    24	        Severity = 'Medium',
    25	        UserImpact = 'High',
    26	        ImplementationCost = 'High',
    27	        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
    28	        Control = 'cisa-scuba:MS.AAD.3.7',
    29	        Service = 'Graph',
    30	        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
    31	        Author = 'soulemike',
    32	        Contributor = 'michaelmsonne'
    33	    )]
    34	    [CmdletBinding()]
    35	    [OutputType([bool])]
    36	    param(
    37	        # Do not check if Hybrid Joined devices are accepted.
    38	        [switch]$SkipHybridJoinCheck
    39	    )
    40	
    41	    $result = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy | Where-Object { $_.state -eq "enabled" }
    42	
    43	    if($SkipHybridJoinCheck){
    44	        $policies = $result | Where-Object {`
    45	            $_.conditions.applications.includeApplications -contains "All" -and `
    46	            $_.conditions.users.includeUsers -contains "All" -and `
    47	            $_.grantControls.builtInControls -contains "compliantDevice" }
    48	    }else{
    49	        $policies = $result | Where-Object {`
    50	            $_.conditions.applications.includeApplications -contains "All" -and `
    51	            $_.conditions.users.includeUsers -contains "All" -and `
    52	            $_.grantControls.builtInControls -contains "compliantDevice" -and `
    53	            $_.grantControls.builtInControls -contains "domainJoinedDevice" -and `
    54	            $_.grantControls.operator -eq "OR" }
    55	    }
    56	
    57	    $testResult = ($policies|Measure-Object).Count -ge 1
    58	
    59	    if ($testResult -and $SkipHybridJoinCheck) {
    60	        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done, your security posture is more than CISA's recommended control. Your tenant has one or more policies that require a compliant device:`n`n%TestResult%"
    61	    } elseif ($testResult) {
    62	        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Your tenant has one or more policies that require a compliant or domain joined device:`n`n%TestResult%"
    63	    } else {
    64	        $testResultMarkdown = "Your tenant does not have any Conditional Access policies that require managed devices."
    65	    }
    66	    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown -GraphObjectType ConditionalAccess -GraphObjects $policies
    67	
    68	    return $testResult
    69	}
﻿Managed devices SHOULD be required for authentication.

Rationale: The security risk of an adversary authenticating to the tenant from their own device is reduced by requiring a managed device to authenticate. Managed devices are under the provisioning and control of the agency. [OMB-22-09](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/2022/01/M-22-09.pdf) states, "When authorizing users to access resources, agencies must consider at least one device-level signal alongside identity information about the authenticated user."

#### Remediation action:

Create a Conditional Access policy requiring a user's device to be either Microsoft Entra hybrid joined or compliant during authentication. Configure the following policy settings in the new Conditional Access policy, per the values below:

1. In **Entra** under **Protection** and **Conditional Access**, select **[Policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies/fromNav/)**.
2. Click on **New policy**
3. Under **New Conditional Access policy**, configure the following policy settings in the new Conditional Access policy, per the values below:
    * Users > Include > **All users**
    * Target resources > Cloud apps > **All cloud apps**
    * Access controls > Grant > Grant Access > **Require device to be marked as compliant** and **Require Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device** > For multiple controls > **Require one of the selected controls**
4. Click **Save**.

#### Related links

* [Entra admin center - Conditional Access | Policies](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies/fromNav/)
* [CISA Strong Authentication & Secure Registration - MS.AAD.3.7v1](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/PowerShell/ScubaGear/baselines/aad.md#msaad37v1)
* [CISA ScubaGear Rego Reference](https://github.com/cisagov/ScubaGear/blob/main/PowerShell/ScubaGear/Rego/AADConfig.rego#L397)

1	﻿function Test-MtCaDeviceComplianceAdminsExists {
     2	  <#
     3	    .Synopsis
     4	    Checks if the tenant has at least one Conditional Access policy requiring device compliance for admins.
     5	
     6	    .Description
     7	    Device compliance Conditional Access policy can be used to require devices to be compliant or hybrid Azure AD joined for admins.
     8	    This is a good way to prevent AITM attacks.
     9	
    10	    Learn more:
    11	    https://aka.ms/CATemplatesAdminDevices
    12	
    13	    .Example
    14	    Test-MtCaDeviceComplianceAdminsExists
    15	
    16	    .LINK
    17	    https://maester.dev/docs/commands/Test-MtCaDeviceComplianceAdminsExists
    18	    #>
    19	  [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseSingularNouns', '', Justification = 'Exists is not a plural.')]
    20	  [Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.SuppressMessageAttribute('PSUseDeclaredVarsMoreThanAssignments', '', Justification = 'PSScriptAnalyzer bug is not detecting usage of PolicyIncludesAllRoles')]
    21	  [MaesterTest(
    22	      Id = 'MT.1014',
    23	      Title = 'At least one Conditional Access policy is configured to require compliant or Entra hybrid joined devices for admins.',
    24	      Product = 'entra',
    25	      Feature = 'conditional-access',
    26	      Area = 'privileged-access',
    27	      ResourceType = 'Tenant',
    28	      Severity = 'High',
    29	      UserImpact = 'Low',
    30	      ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
    31	      Mitre = ('T1078.004', 'T1539', 'T1557'),
    32	      Control = ('nist-800-53-r5:IA-3', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-2(11)'),
    33	      Service = 'Graph',
    34	      License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
    35	      Author = 'f-bader',
    36	      Contributor = ('RetroDadson', 'l-gosling')
    37	  )]
    38	  [CmdletBinding()]
    39	  [OutputType([bool])]
    40	  param ()
    41	
    42	  $AdministrativeRolesToCheck = @(
    43	    '62e90394-69f5-4237-9190-012177145e10', # Global Administrator
    44	    '9b895d92-2cd3-44c7-9d02-a6ac2d5ea5c3', # Application Administrator
    45	    'c4e39bd9-1100-46d3-8c65-fb160da0071f', # Authentication Administrator
    46	    'b0f54661-2d74-4c50-afa3-1ec803f12efe', # Billing Administrator
    47	    '158c047a-c907-4556-b7ef-446551a6b5f7', # Cloud Application Administrator
    48	    'b1be1c3e-b65d-4f19-8427-f6fa0d97feb9', # Conditional Access Administrator
    49	    '29232cdf-9323-42fd-ade2-1d097af3e4de', # Exchange Administrator
    50	    '729827e3-9c14-49f7-bb1b-9608f156bbb8', # Helpdesk Administrator
    51	    '966707d0-3269-4727-9be2-8c3a10f19b9d', # Password Administrator
    52	    '7be44c8a-adaf-4e2a-84d6-ab2649e08a13', # Privileged Authentication Administrator
    53	    'e8611ab8-c189-46e8-94e1-60213ab1f814', # Privileged Role Administrator
    54	    '194ae4cb-b126-40b2-bd5b-6091b380977d', # Security Administrator
    55	    'f28a1f50-f6e7-4571-818b-6a12f2af6b6c', # SharePoint Administrator
    56	    'fe930be7-5e62-47db-91af-98c3a49a38b1'  # User Administrator
    57	  )
    58	
    59	  $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy | Where-Object { $_.state -eq 'enabled' }
    60	
    61	  $testDescription = '
    62	Microsoft recommends requiring device compliance for administrators that are members of the following roles:
    63	
    64	* Global Administrator
    65	* Application Administrator
    66	* Authentication Administrator
    67	* Billing Administrator
    68	* Cloud Application Administrator
    69	* Conditional Access Administrator
    70	* Exchange Administrator
    71	* Helpdesk Administrator
    72	* Password Administrator
    73	* Privileged Authentication Administrator
    74	* Privileged Role Administrator
    75	* Security Administrator
    76	* SharePoint Administrator
    77	* User Administrator
    78	
    79	See [Require compliant or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device for administrators - Microsoft Learn](https://aka.ms/CATemplatesAdminDevices)'
    80	  $testResult = "These Conditional Access policies require compliant or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device for administrators:`n`n"
    81	
    82	  $result = $false
    83	  foreach ($policy in $policies) {
    84	    $PolicyIncludesAllRoles = $true
    85	    $AdministrativeRolesToCheck | ForEach-Object {
    86	      if ( ( $_ -notin $policy.conditions.users.includeRoles -and $policy.conditions.users.includeUsers -notcontains 'All' ) -or
    87	        $_ -in $policy.conditions.users.excludeRoles
    88	      ) {
    89	        $PolicyIncludesAllRoles = $false
    90	      }
    91	    }
    92	
    93	    $builtInControls = @($policy.grantControls.builtInControls)
    94	    $deviceControls = @('compliantDevice', 'domainJoinedDevice')
    95	    $hasDeviceControl = @($builtInControls | Where-Object { $_ -in $deviceControls }).Count -gt 0
    96	    $hasNonDeviceControl = @($builtInControls | Where-Object { $_ -notin $deviceControls }).Count -gt 0
    97	    $requiresDeviceControl = $hasDeviceControl -and (-not $hasNonDeviceControl -or $policy.grantControls.operator -eq 'AND')
    98	
    99	    if ( $requiresDeviceControl -and
   100	      $PolicyIncludesAllRoles -and
   101	      $policy.conditions.applications.includeApplications -eq 'All'
   102	    ) {
   103	      Write-Verbose -Message "Found a Conditional Access policy requiring device compliance for admins: $($policy.displayName)"
   104	      $testResult += "  - [$(Get-MtSafeMarkdown $policy.displayName)](https://entra.microsoft.com/#view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/PolicyBlade/policyId/$($($policy.id))?%23view/Microsoft_AAD_ConditionalAccess/ConditionalAccessBlade/~/Policies?=)`n"
   105	      $result = $true
   106	    }
   107	  }
   108	
   109	  if ($result -eq $false) {
   110	    $testResult = 'There was no Conditional Access policy requiring compliant or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined device for administrators.'
   111	  }
   112	  Add-MtTestResultDetail -Description $testDescription -Result $testResult
   113	
   114	  return $result
   115	}

Devices evaluate the rules in the policy to report a device compliance status. A noncompliant status can result in one or more actions for noncompliance. Microsoft Entra Conditional Access policies can also use that status to block access to organizational resources from that device.

Important

Before you set up Conditional Access, you'll need to set up Intune device compliance policies to evaluate devices based on whether they meet specific requirements. See [Get started with device compliance policies in Intune](../compliance/create-policy).

## How this works

Device-based Conditional Access uses compliance status signals from Intune to enforce access controls in Microsoft Entra ID. Configuration involves two phases:

- Phase 1 - Configure device compliance policies in Intune: These policies evaluate whether managed devices meet your security requirements. Intune reports that compliance status to Microsoft Entra ID.
- Phase 2 - Create a Conditional Access policy in Microsoft Entra: The policy uses the compliance signal from Intune. This article shows you how to configure the policy from within the Microsoft Intune admin center.

## Create the Conditional Access policy

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Intune admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431).
2. Select **Endpoint security** > **Conditional Access** > **Create new policy**.

    The **New** pane opens, which is the configuration pane from Microsoft Entra. The policy you’re creating is a Microsoft Entra policy for Conditional Access. To learn more about this pane and Conditional Access policies, see [Conditional Access policy components](/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policies) in the Microsoft Entra content.
3. Under **Assignments**, configure **Users and groups** to select the Identities in the directory that the policy applies to. To learn more, see [Users and groups](/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-users-groups) in the Microsoft Entra documentation.

    - On the **Include** tab, configure the user and groups you want to include.
    - Use the **Exclude** tab if there are any users, roles, or groups you want to exclude from this policy.

    Tip

    Test the policy against a smaller group of users to make sure it works as expected before deploying it to larger groups.
4. Next configure **Target resources**, which is also under *Assignments*. Use the drop-down for *Select what this policy applies to* to select **Cloud apps**.

49:Simplify device enrollment by enabling *automatic enrollment* in Microsoft Intune. This enrollment method enables devices to enroll automatically when they join or register in Microsoft Entra ID. Enrollment in Intune occurs when:

81:## Enable Windows automatic enrollment
91:5. Configure the **MDM user scope** for Microsoft Intune. This setting enables automatic MDM enrollment for Microsoft Entra users so that you can manage their devices in Intune.
93:![Screenshot shows the Microsoft Entra MDM user scope.](media/enable-automatic-mdm/auto-enroll-scope.png)
97:    - **None** - Automatic MDM enrollment is disabled for all users. You can still manage devices in Microsoft Intune but users must initiate MDM enrollment.
98:    - **Some** - Automatic MDM enrollment is enabled for the users you select.
99:    - **All** - Automatic MDM enrollment is enabled for all users. Their devices automatically enroll in Intune when they join or register with Microsoft Entra ID.
103:    If your intent is to enable automatic MDM enrollment for Windows BYOD devices, select **All** or **Some** for the MDM user scope. Then make sure the WIP user scope is **None** or **Some**, and that users are not members of both user scopes.
109:7. You have the option to control if users in an automatic enrollment configuration on Microsoft Entra registered devices are prompted to MDM enroll their device in the work or school account registration flow (referring to [Add Your Work or School Account to a Windows Device](https://support.microsoft.com/windows/add-your-work-or-school-account-to-a-windows-device-a6505ceb-1a20-4b15-889c-250175481506)). To control the behavior of the flow, use the **Disable MDM enrollment when adding work or school account** setting.

130:    When a user is in both the MDM user scope and WIP user scope:

For more information, see [Unlicensed admins](../../fundamentals/licensing#unlicensed-admin-access).

[MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CIS.M365.4.1',
        Title = 'Ensure devices without a compliance policy are marked ''not compliant''',
        Product = 'intune',
        Feature = 'device-compliance',
        Area = 'devices',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = 'T1078.004',
        Control = ('cis-m365:4.1', 'nist-800-53-r5:AC-19', 'nist-800-53-r5:CM-6'),
        Step = 'intune.mark-unassigned-noncompliant',
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'INTUNE_A',
        Author = 'oed-metzb',
        Contributor = ('Mynster9361', 'Korthal-Maiyn')
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    Write-Verbose 'Getting settings...'
    $settings = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "deviceManagement/settings"

    Write-Verbose 'Executing checks'
    $checkSecureByDefault = $settings | Where-Object { $_.secureByDefault -eq $true }

    $testResult = (($checkSecureByDefault | Measure-Object).Count -ge 1)

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. Your tenant settings comply with CIS recommendations.`n`n%TestResult%"
    }
    else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Your tenant settings do not comply with CIS recommendations.`n`n%TestResult%"
    }

    $resultMd = "| Setting | Result |`n"
    $resultMd += "| --- | --- |`n"

    if ($checkSecureByDefault) {
        $checkSecureByDefaultResult = '✅ Pass'
    }
    else {
        $checkSecureByDefaultResult = '❌ Fail'
    }

    $resultMd += "| Mark devices with no compliance policy assigned as 'Not compliant' | $checkSecureByDefaultResult |`n"
    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace '%TestResult%', $resultMd

50 # How Token Protection Enhances Conditional Access Policies - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn
51
52 ## Overview
53 
54 Token Protection is a Conditional Access session control that attempts to reduce token replay attacks by ensuring only device bound sign-in session tokens, like [Primary Refresh Tokens (PRTs)](../devices/concept-primary-refresh-token), are accepted by Microsoft Entra ID when applications request access to protected resources.
55 
56 When a user registers a supported device with Microsoft Entra, a PRT is issued and cryptographically bound to that device. This binding ensures that even if a threat actor steals the token, it can't be used from another device. With Token Protection enforced, Microsoft Entra validates that only these bound sign-in session tokens are used by supported applications.
57 
58 Note
59 
60 Use Token Protection as part of a broader defense-in-depth strategy against token theft. For more information, see [Protecting tokens in Microsoft Entra](../devices/protecting-tokens-microsoft-entra-id).
61 
62 ## Platform availability
63 
64 | Platform | Native applications | Browser-based applications |
65 | --- | --- | --- |
66 | Windows | Generally Available | Preview for supported web apps that access Azure Resource Manager |
67 | iOS / iPadOS | Generally Available | Not supported |
68 | macOS | Generally Available | Preview for supported web apps that access Azure Resource Manager |
69 
70 Note
71 
72 Browser-based application support is currently limited to selected web apps, browsers, and device configurations that access Azure Resource Manager. For requirements and the list of supported applications, see [Token Protection deployment guide - Web apps](deployment-guide-token-protection-web-apps).
73 
74 ## Supported resources
75 
76 For native applications, Token Protection policy can be enforced on the following cloud resources:
77 
78 - Exchange Online
79 - SharePoint Online
80 - Microsoft Teams
81 
82 On Windows, enforcement is also supported for:
83 
84 - Azure Virtual Desktop
85 - Windows 365
86 
87 For browser-based applications in preview, enforcement is supported for Azure Resource Manager, configured in Conditional Access as the **Windows Azure Service Management API** resource. Only selected web applications that access Azure Resource Manager are supported. For details, see [Token Protection deployment guide - Web apps](deployment-guide-token-protection-web-apps).
88 
89 ### Supported devices
90 
91 **Windows**:
92 
93 - Windows 10 or newer devices that are Microsoft Entra joined, Microsoft Entra hybrid joined, or Microsoft Entra registered. See the known limitations section in the appropriate deployment guide for unsupported device types.
94 - Windows Server 2019 or newer that are hybrid Microsoft Entra joined.
95 - For detailed steps on how to register your device, see [Register your personal device on your work or school network](https://support.microsoft.com/account-billing/register-your-personal-device-on-your-work-or-school-network-8803dd61-a613-45e3-ae6c-bd1ab25bf8a8).
96 - Browser-based application support (Preview) has additional operating system, browser, extension, and configuration requirements. See [Token Protection deployment guide - Web apps](deployment-guide-token-protection-web-apps).
97 
98 **Apple (Preview)**:
99 
100 - macOS 14.0 or later. Requires the Microsoft Enterprise single sign-on (SSO) plug-in. Alternatively, you can also use Platform SSO. Only MDM-managed devices are supported.
101 - iOS / iPadOS 16.0 or later. Requires the Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in. Only MDM-managed devices are supported.
102 - For detailed steps on how to set up, see [Enabling Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in](../../identity-platform/apple-sso-plugin) and configuring [Platform SSO for macOS](/en-us/intune/intune-service/configuration/platform-sso-macos).
103 - Browser-based application support (Preview) on macOS has additional browser, extension, and configuration requirements. See [Token Protection deployment guide - Web apps](deployment-guide-token-protection-web-apps).
104 
105 ## Deployment
106 
107 To minimize the likelihood of user disruption due to app or device incompatibility, follow these recommendations:
108 
109 - Start with a pilot group of users and expand over time.
110 - Create a Conditional Access policy in [report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only) before enforcing token protection.
111 - Capture both interactive and non-interactive sign-in logs.
112 - Analyze these logs long enough to cover normal application use.
113 - Add known, reliable users to an enforcement policy.
114 
115 This process helps assess your users' client and app compatibility for token protection enforcement.
116 
117 ### Deployment guides
118 
119 Select the guide for your target platform:
120 
121 - **Windows**: [Token Protection deployment guide - Windows](deployment-guide-token-protection-windows)
122 - **iOS, iPadOS, and macOS**: [Token Protection deployment guide - Apple](deployment-guide-token-protection-apple)

content.content:
## Overview

This guide covers the steps required to deploy and enforce Token Protection for sign-in session tokens on Windows platform.

For an overview of Token Protection and supported platforms, see [Token Protection in Microsoft Entra Conditional Access](concept-token-protection). Review the overview documentation before using this deployment guide.

93 ### Known limitations
94 
95 - Office perpetual clients version 2024 and later support Token Protection. Versions earlier than 2024 aren't supported.
96 - The following applications don't support signing in using protected token flows and users are blocked when accessing Exchange and SharePoint:
97 - PowerShell modules accessing SharePoint
98 - PowerQuery extension for Excel for users not in Current Channel updates
99 - Extensions to Visual Studio Code which access Exchange or SharePoint
100 - The following Windows client devices aren't supported:
101 - Surface Hub
102 - Windows-based Microsoft Teams Rooms (MTR) systems
103 - [External users](/en-us/entra/external-id/what-is-b2b) who meet the token protection device registration requirements in their home tenant are supported. However, users who don't meet these requirements see an unclear error message with no indication of the root cause.
104 - Devices registered with Microsoft Entra ID using the following methods are unsupported:
105 - Microsoft Entra joined [Azure Virtual Desktop session hosts](/en-us/azure/virtual-desktop/azure-ad-joined-session-hosts).
106 - Windows devices deployed using [bulk enrollment](/en-us/mem/intune-service/enrollment/windows-bulk-enroll).
107 - [Cloud PCs deployed by Windows 365](/en-us/windows-365/enterprise/identity-authentication#device-join-types) that are Microsoft Entra joined.
108 - Power Automate hosted machine groups that are [Microsoft Entra joined](/en-us/power-automate/desktop-flows/hosted-machine-groups#general-network-requirements).
109 - Windows Autopilot devices deployed using [self-deploying mode](/en-us/autopilot/self-deploying).
110 - Windows virtual machines deployed in Azure using the virtual machine (VM) extension that are enabled for [Microsoft Entra ID authentication](/en-us/entra/identity/devices/howto-vm-sign-in-azure-ad-windows).
111 
112 To identify the impacted devices due to unsupported registration types listed previously, inspect the `tokenProtectionStatusDetails` attribute in the sign-in logs. Token requests that are blocked due to an unsupported device registration type, can be identified with a `signInSessionStatusCode` value of 1003.
113 
114 To prevent disruption during onboarding, modify the token protection Conditional Access policy by adding a device filter condition that excludes devices in the previously described deployment category. For example, to exclude:
115 
116 - Cloud PCs that are Microsoft Entra joined, you can use `systemLabels -eq "CloudPC" and trustType -eq "AzureAD"`.
117 - Azure Virtual Desktops that are Microsoft Entra joined, you can use `systemLabels -eq "AzureVirtualDesktop" and trustType -eq "AzureAD"`.
118 - Power Automate hosted machine groups that are Microsoft Entra joined, you can use `systemLabels -eq "MicrosoftPowerAutomate" and trustType -eq "AzureAD"`.
119 - Windows Autopilot devices deployed using self-deploying mode, you can use enrollmentProfileName property. As an example, if you created an enrollment profile in Intune for your Autopilot self-deployment mode devices as "Autopilot self-deployment profile," you can use `enrollmentProfileName -eq "Autopilot self-deployment profile"`.
120 - Windows virtual machines in Azure that are Microsoft Entra joined, you can use `profileType -eq "SecureVM" and trustType -eq "AzureAD"`.
121 
122 ## How to enable Token Protection on Windows
123 
124 For users, the deployment of a Conditional Access policy to enforce token protection should be invisible when using compatible client platforms on registered devices and compatible applications.
125 
126 To minimize the likelihood of user disruption due to app or device incompatibility, follow these recommendations:
127 
128 - Start with a pilot group of users and expand over time.
129 - Create a Conditional Access policy in [report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only) before enforcing token protection.
130 - Capture both interactive and non-interactive sign-in logs.
131 - Analyze these logs long enough to cover normal application use.
132 - Add known, reliable users to an enforcement policy.
133 
134 This process helps assess your users' client and app compatibility for token protection enforcement.
135 
136 ## Create a Conditional Access policy
137 
138 Users who perform specialized roles like those described in [Privileged access security levels](/en-us/security/privileged-access-workstations/privileged-access-security-levels#specialized) are possible targets for this functionality. Pilot with a small subset to begin.
139 
140 The following steps help you create a Conditional Access policy to require token protection for Exchange Online and SharePoint Online on Windows devices.
141 
142 1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
143 2. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**.
144 3. Select **New policy**.
145 4. Give your policy a name. Create a meaningful standard for the names of your policies.
146 5. Under **Assignments**, select **Users or workload identities**.
147 1. Under **Include**, select the users or groups who are testing this policy.
148 2. Under **Exclude**, select **Users and groups** and choose your organization's emergency access or break-glass accounts.
149 6. Under **Target resources** > **Resources (formerly cloud apps)** > **Include** > **Select resources**
150 1. Under **Select**, select the following applications:
151 
152 1. Office 365 Exchange Online
153 2. Office 365 SharePoint Online
154 3. Microsoft Teams Services
155 4. If you deployed Windows App in your environment, include:
156 1. Azure Virtual Desktop
157 2. Windows 365
158 3. Windows Cloud Login
159 
160 Warning
161 
162 Your Conditional Access policy should only be configured for these applications. Selecting the **Office 365** application group might result in unintended failures. This change is an exception to the general rule that the **Office 365** application group should be selected in a Conditional Access policy.
163 2. Choose **Select**.
164 7. Under **Conditions**:
165 1. Under **Device platforms**:
166 1. Set **Configure** to **Yes**.
167 2. **Include** > **Select device platforms** > **Windows**.
168 3. Select **Done**.
169 2. Under **Client apps**:
170 1. Set **Configure** to **Yes**.
171 
172 Warning
173 
174 Not configuring the **Client Apps** condition, or leaving **Browser** selected might cause applications that use MSAL.js, such as Teams Web to be blocked.
175 2. Under Modern authentication clients, only select **Mobile apps and desktop clients**. Leave other items unchecked.
176 3. Select **Done**.
177 8. Under **Access controls** > **Session**, select **Require token protection for sign-in sessions** and select **Select**.
178 9. Confirm your settings and set **Enable policy** to **Report-only**.
179 10. Select **Create** to enable your policy.
180 
181 After confirming your settings using [policy impact or report-only mode](concept-conditional-access-report-only#reviewing-results), move the **Enable policy** toggle from **Report-only** to **On**.
182 
183 Tip
184 
185 Because Conditional Access policies requiring token protection are currently only available for Windows and Apple devices, it's necessary to secure your environment against potential policy bypass when an attacker might appear to come from a different platform.
186 
187 In addition, you should configure the following policies:
188 
189 - [Block access from unknown platforms](policy-all-users-device-unknown-unsupported)
190 - [Require device compliance for all known platforms](policy-all-users-device-compliance)
191 
192 ## Capture logs and analyze

## Capture logs and analyze

Monitor Conditional Access enforcement of token protection before and after enforcement by using features like [Policy impact](concept-conditional-access-report-only#policy-impact), Sign-in logs, and Log Analytics.

### Sign-in logs

Use Microsoft Entra sign-in log to verify the outcome of a token protection enforcement policy in report only mode or in enabled mode.

[![Screenshot showing an example of a policy not being satisfied.](media/deployment-guide-token-protection-windows/sign-in-log-sample.png)](media/deployment-guide-token-protection-windows/sign-in-log-sample.png#lightbox)

1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
2. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Monitoring & health** > **Sign-in logs**.
3. Select a specific request to determine if the policy is applied or not.
4. Go to the **Conditional Access** or **Report-Only** pane depending on its state and select the name of your policy requiring token protection.
5. Under **Session Controls** check to see if the policy requirements were satisfied or not.
6. To find more details about the binding state of the request, select the pane **Basic Info** and see the field **Token Protection - Sign In Session**. Possible values are:
    1. Bound: the request was using bound protocols. Some sign-ins might include multiple requests, and all requests must be bound to satisfy the token protection policy. Even if an individual request appears to be bound, it doesn't ensure compliance with the policy if other requests are unbound. To see all requests for a sign-in, you can filter all requests for a specific user or look by correlation ID.
    2. Unbound: the request wasn't using bound protocols. Possible `statusCodes`when request is unbound are:
        1. 1002: The request is unbound due to the lack of Microsoft Entra ID device state.
        2. 1003: The request is unbound because the Microsoft Entra ID device state doesn't satisfy Conditional Access policy requirements for token protection. This error could be due to an unsupported device registration type, or the device wasn't registered using fresh sign-in credentials.
        3. 1005: The request is unbound for other unspecified reasons.
        4. 1006: The request is unbound because the OS version is unsupported.
        5. 1008: The request is unbound because the client isn't integrated with the platform broker, such as Windows Account Manager (WAM).

[![Screenshot showing a sample sign-in with the Token Protection - Sign In Session attribute highlighted. ](media/deployment-guide-token-protection-windows/sign-in-log-sample-unbound-status-code-1002.png)](media/deployment-guide-token-protection-windows/sign-in-log-sample-unbound-status-code-1002.png#lightbox)

Note

**Sign-in logs output:** The value of the string used in `enforcedSessionControls` and `sessionControlsNotSatisfied` changed from `Binding` to `SignInTokenProtection` in late June 2023. Queries on sign-in log data should be updated to reflect this change. The examples cover both values to include historical data.

### Log Analytics
## End user experience

A user that registered or enrolled their supported device doesn't experience any differences in the sign in experience on a token protection supported application when the token protection requirement is enabled.

A user who hasn't registered or enrolled their device and if the token protection policy is enabled will be prompted to register the device.

![Screenshot of the token protection register in line screen.](media/deployment-guide-token-protection-windows/token-protection-register-prompt.png)

For users who have not yet updated to the latest September 2026 Windows update will continue to see the below message:

![Screenshot of the token protection error message when your device isn't registered or enrolled.](media/deployment-guide-token-protection-windows/token-protection-register-or-enroll-device.png)

A user that isn't using a supported application when the token protection policy is enabled will see the following screenshot after authenticating.

## Prerequisites

Using this feature requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses. To find the right license for your requirements, see [Compare generally available features of Microsoft Entra ID](https://www.microsoft.com/security/business/identity-access-management/azure-ad-pricing).

## Supported applications and resources

Before enforcing the policy, ensure users are running supported and up-to-date client versions. Older or out-of-support versions might not be compatible and can be blocked.

### Applications

Token Protection can be applied to the following applications:

- Exchange PowerShell module
- Microsoft Copilot
- Microsoft Edge (support for sign-in to Edge profile only)\*
- Microsoft Graph PowerShell with [EnableLoginByWAM](/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.graph.authentication/set-mggraphoption#example-1-set-web-account-manager-support) option
- Microsoft Loop
- Microsoft Teams
- Microsoft To Do
- OneNote
- OneDrive
- Outlook
- Power BI desktop
- PowerQuery extension for Excel (only available for users on [Current Channel](/en-us/microsoft-365-apps/updates/overview-update-channels#current-channel-overview))
- Visual Studio Code
- Visual Studio when using the 'Windows authentication broker' Sign-in option
- Windows App
- Word, Excel, PowerPoint

\*Token Protection currently supports native applications only. Browser-based applications are not supported.

### Resources

Token Protection on Windows platforms can be used to protect the following resources:

- Exchange Online
- SharePoint Online
- Microsoft Teams
- Azure Virtual Desktop
- Windows 365

content.content:
## Overview

This guide covers the steps required to deploy and enforce Token Protection for sign-in session tokens on Apple platforms (iOS, iPadOS, and macOS).

Before using this deployment guide, review [Token Protection in Microsoft Entra Conditional Access](concept-token-protection) for an overview of the feature and supported platforms.

Important

Apple's native Mail and Calendar apps don't support Token Protection. Users will be blocked from accessing resources protected by Token Protection when the policy is enforced. Communicate this behavior to affected users before deployment.

## Prerequisites
92 ### Known Limitations
93 
94 - Token Protection currently requires the Microsoft Enterprise single-sign-on (SSO) plug-in, which requires Mobile Device Management (MDM). *Unmanaged iOS and macOS devices aren't supported at this time.*
95 - *Apple's native Mail and Calendar apps don't support Token Protection.* Users will be blocked from accessing resources protected by Token Protection when the policy is enforced.
96 - In report-only mode, requests that don't use hardware-backed device registration appear as noncompliant, even if the user is eligible for an upgrade to hardware-backed device registration. Use sign-in logs and status codes to assess true readiness. See the Review readiness with logs and metrics section.
97 - The **Token Protection – Sign-in Session** column in sign-in logs shows all requests without hardware-backed device identity as "Unbound." These logs include requests from users who are eligible to upgrade their registration.
98 - [External users](../../external-id/what-is-b2b) who meet the token protection device registration requirements in their home tenant are supported. Users who don't meet these requirements will see an error message with no clear indication of the root cause.
99 
100 ## How to enable Token Protection on Apple platforms
101 
102 Unlike Windows, Apple platforms don't use a Trusted Platform Module (TPM). Instead, Microsoft Entra ID uses Apple Secure Enclave to store proof-of-possession keys. On macOS devices without Secure Enclave (for example, some older Mac mini models), Microsoft Entra ID falls back to an enhanced version of the Apple Keychain (Data Protection Keychain).
103 
104 This difference means that some prerequisite configuration is required before users can register devices in a way that supports Token Protection enforcement.
105 
106 The high-level steps to enable Token Protection on Apple platforms are as follows:
107 
108 1. Configure hardware-backed device registration
109 2. Configure the report-only Conditional Access policy
110 3. Review readiness with logs and metrics
111 4. Enforce the policy
112 
113 ## Configure hardware-backed device registration
114 
115 Complete the following steps for *each* platform you're deploying to. These steps must be completed *before* users register their devices.
116 
117 Note
118 
119 Users who registered their devices before these steps were completed will be prompted to enter their credentials the first time they access a resource protected by the Token Protection policy. Once they complete authentication successfully, their device registration is automatically upgraded to hardware-backed storage. For more information, see **Upgrade device registration**.
120 
121 # [iOS and iPadOS](#tab/ios-and-ipados)
122 1. Install Microsoft Authenticator from the Apple App Store, or deploy it via your MDM solution. Authenticator serves as the authentication broker for Microsoft Entra sign-ins.
123 2. Enable hardware-backed registration using the [Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in for Apple Devices](../../identity-platform/apple-sso-plugin).
124 
125 # [macOS](#tab/macos)
126 1. Install the Microsoft Company Portal or deploy it via your MDM solution. Company Portal serves as the authentication broker for Microsoft Entra sign-ins.
127 2. Enable hardware-backed registration using one of the following options:
128 - Option A: Enable the [Microsoft Enterprise SSO plug-in for Apple Devices](../../identity-platform/apple-sso-plugin).
129 - Option B: Configure **Platform SSO for macOS**. For setup instructions, see [Configure Platform SSO for macOS devices in Microsoft Intune](/en-us/intune/intune-service/configuration/platform-sso-macos).
130 
131 ---
132 
133 ## Configure the report-only mode policy
134 
135 Before enforcing the policy, deploy it in report-only mode to assess the effect and identify noncompliant sign-in sessions.
136 
137 1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
138 2. Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Policies**.
139 3. Give your policy a name. Create a meaningful standard for the names of your policies.
140 4. Under **Assignments**, select **Users, agents, or workload identities**.
141 1. Under **Include**, select the users or groups to target.
142 2. Under **Exclude**, select **Users and groups** and choose your organization's emergency access or break-glass accounts.
143 5. Under **Target resources** > **Resources (formerly cloud apps)** > **Include** > **Select resources**
144 1. Under **Select**, select the following applications:
145 
146 1. Office 365 Exchange Online
147 2. Office 365 SharePoint Online
148 
149 Warning
150 
151 Your Conditional Access policy should only be configured for these applications. Selecting the **Office 365** application group might result in unintended failures. This change is an exception to the general rule that the **Office 365** application group should be selected in a Conditional Access policy.
152 2. Choose **Select**.
153 6. Under **Conditions**:
154 1. Under **Device platforms**:
155 1. Set **Configure** to **Yes**.
156 2. **Include** > **Select device platforms** > **iOS** and **macOS**.
157 3. Select **Done**.
158 2. Under **Client apps**:
159 1. Set **Configure** to **Yes**.
160 
161 Warning
162 
163 Not configuring the **Client Apps** condition, or leaving **Browser** selected might cause applications that use MSAL.js, such as Teams Web to be blocked.
164 2. Under Modern authentication clients, only select **Mobile apps and desktop clients**. Leave other items unchecked.
165 3. Select **Done**.
166 7. Under **Access controls** > **Session**, select **Require token protection for sign-in sessions** and select **Select**.
167 8. Confirm your settings and set **Enable policy** to **Report-only**.
168 9. Select **Create** to enable your policy.
169 
170 Tip
171 
172 Because Conditional Access policies requiring token protection are currently only available for Windows and Apple devices, it's necessary to secure your environment against potential policy bypass when an attacker might appear to come from a different platform.
173 
174 In addition, you should configure the following policies:
175 
176 - [Block access from unknown platforms](policy-all-users-device-unknown-unsupported)
177 - [Require device compliance for all known platforms](policy-all-users-device-compliance)
178 
179 ## Review readiness with logs and metrics

[MaesterTest(
        Id = 'CIS.M365.5.2.2.16',
        Title = 'Ensure Token Protection is enforced for session tokens',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'conditional-access',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'Medium',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Medium',
        Mitre = 'T1550.004',
        Control = ('cis-m365:5.2.2.16', 'nist-800-53-r5:SC-23'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        License = 'AAD_PREMIUM',
        Author = 'JeremyFinney-lgtm'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    Write-Verbose 'Getting Conditional Access policies...'
    $policies = Get-MtConditionalAccessPolicy
    $requiredApps = @(
        '00000002-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000'  # Office 365 Exchange Online
        '00000003-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000'  # Office 365 SharePoint Online
        'cc15fd57-2c6c-4117-a88c-83b1d56b4bbe'  # Microsoft Teams Services
    )

    $candidates = @($policies | Where-Object { $_.sessionControls.secureSignInSession.isEnabled })

    $report = foreach ($policy in $candidates) {
        $includedApps = @($policy.conditions.applications.includeApplications)
        $missingApps = @($requiredApps | Where-Object { $includedApps -notcontains $_ })
        $problems = @(Get-MtCisConditionalAccessScopeProblem -Policy $policy -Users NotNone -Applications $requiredApps -TargetedCondition Platforms, ClientAppTypes)
        $checks = [ordered]@{
            'Scope covers the required users and apps' = $problems.Count -eq 0
            'Exchange, SharePoint and Teams'           = $missingApps.Count -eq 0
            'Windows platform'                         = @($policy.conditions.platforms.includePlatforms) -contains 'windows'
            'Desktop clients'                          = (@($policy.conditions.clientAppTypes) | Sort-Object) -join ',' -eq 'mobileAppsAndDesktopClients'
            'Token protection enabled'                 = $policy.sessionControls.secureSignInSession.isEnabled -eq $true
            'Enabled'                                  = $policy.state -eq 'enabled'
        }
        $failed = @($checks.GetEnumerator() | Where-Object { -not $_.Value } | ForEach-Object { $_.Key })
        $failedText = $failed -join ', '
        if ($problems.Count -gt 0) { $failedText += " ($($problems -join '; '))" }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $policy.displayName; State = $policy.state; Failed = $failedText; Pass = $failed.Count -eq 0 }
    }
    $testResult = @($report | Where-Object { $_.Pass }).Count -gt 0
    $passText = 'An enabled Conditional Access policy enforces token protection for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Microsoft Teams.'
    $failText = if ($candidates.Count -eq 0) { 'No Conditional Access policy that uses token protection was found.' } else { 'No enabled Conditional Access policy enforces token protection for Exchange Online, SharePoint Online and Microsoft Teams on Windows.' }

    $resultMd = "| Policy | State | Failed checks | Result |`n"
    $resultMd += "| --- | --- | --- | --- |`n"
    foreach ($row in $report) {
        $resultMd += "| $($row.Name) | $($row.State) | $(if ($row.Failed) { $row.Failed } else { 'None' }) | $(if ($row.Pass) { '✅ Pass' } else { '❌ Fail' }) |`n"
    }

    if ($testResult) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. $passText`n`n%TestResult%"
    }
    else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "$failText`n`n%TestResult%"
    }
    $testResultMarkdown = $testResultMarkdown -replace '%TestResult%', $resultMd

    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Result $testResultMarkdown
    return $testResult
}

# Get all enabled Conditional Access policies
    $policies = Invoke-ZtGraphRequest -RelativeUri "identity/conditionalAccess/policies" -ApiVersion v1.0

    $matchingPolicies = @()

    foreach ($policy in $policies) {
        $appliesToAllUsers = ($policy.conditions.users.includeUsers -contains "All")
        $appliesToAllApps = ($policy.conditions.applications.includeApplications -contains "All")
        $compliantDevice = ($policy.grantControls.builtInControls -contains "compliantDevice")
        $hybridJoinedDevice = ($policy.grantControls.builtInControls -contains "domainJoinedDevice")
        $enabled = $policy.state -eq "enabled"

        if ($compliantDevice -or $hybridJoinedDevice) {
            $status = $enabled -and $appliesToAllUsers -and $appliesToAllApps -and ($compliantDevice -or $hybridJoinedDevice)
            $detail = [PSCustomObject]@{
                PolicyId           = $policy.id
                PolicyState        = $policy.state
                DisplayName        = $policy.displayName
                AllUsers           = $appliesToAllUsers
                AllApps            = $appliesToAllApps
                CompliantDevice    = $compliantDevice
                HybridJoinedDevice = $hybridJoinedDevice
                Status             = $status
            }
            $matchingPolicies += $detail
        }
    }

    $passed = ($matchingPolicies.where{ $_.Status -eq $true } | Measure-Object).Count -gt 0

70:### Who should use Conditional Access?
73:- If your organization has complex security requirements, you should consider [Conditional Access](/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common).
83:- Don't have any Conditional Access policies
87:After this setting is enabled, all users in the organization will need to register for multifactor authentication. To avoid confusion, refer to the email you received and alternatively you can disable security defaults after it's enabled.
89:To configure security defaults in your directory, you must be assigned at least the [Conditional Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator) role.
95:1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](../identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
137:- Conditional Access Administrator

164:*Also available as a [Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy](../identity/conditional-access/managed-policies#upgrade-from-security-defaults) if you disable security defaults.*
183:*Also available as a [Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy](../identity/conditional-access/managed-policies#upgrade-from-security-defaults) if you disable security defaults.*
189:After security defaults are enabled in your tenant, authentication requests that use device code flow are blocked. Applications or devices that depend on device code flow won't be able to complete sign-in while security defaults are enabled. If your organization needs granular control and exceptions, you should consider [Conditional Access](/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common).
219:Exchange Online tenants created before 2017 have modern authentication disabled by default. In order to avoid the possibility of a login loop while authenticating through these tenants, you must [enable modern authentication](/en-us/exchange/clients-and-mobile-in-exchange-online/enable-or-disable-modern-authentication-in-exchange-online).
225:*Also available as a [Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policy](../identity/conditional-access/managed-policies#upgrade-from-security-defaults) if you disable security defaults.*
239:Don't disable methods for your organization if you're using security defaults. Disabling methods might lead to locking yourself out of your tenant. Leave all **Methods available to users** enabled in the [MFA service settings portal](../identity/authentication/howto-mfa-getstarted#choose-authentication-methods-for-mfa).
245:### Disabled MFA status
247:If your organization is a previous user of per-user based multifactor authentication, don't be alarmed to not see users in an **Enabled** or **Enforced** status if you look at the multifactor authentication status page. **Disabled** is the appropriate status for users who are using security defaults or Conditional Access based multifactor authentication.
251:Organizations that choose to implement Conditional Access policies that replace security defaults must disable security defaults.
253:Disable security defaults in your directory:
255:1. Sign in to the [Microsoft Entra admin center](https://entra.microsoft.com) as at least a [Conditional Access Administrator](/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#conditional-access-administrator).
258:4. Set **Security defaults** to **Disabled (not recommended)**.
261:### Move from security defaults to Conditional Access
263:While security defaults are a good baseline to start your security posture from, they don't allow for the customization that many organizations require. Conditional Access policies provide a full range of customization that more complex organizations require.
265:| - | Security defaults | Conditional Access |
272:Organizations who would like to test out the features of Conditional Access can [sign up for a free trial](get-started-premium) to get started.
274:After administrators disable security defaults, organizations should immediately enable Conditional Access policies to protect their organization. [Microsoft-managed Conditional Access policies](../identity/conditional-access/managed-policies#upgrade-from-security-defaults) are available to maintain the same protections, covering blocking legacy authentication, requiring MFA for Azure management, requiring MFA for admins, and requiring MFA for all users. Organizations should review these policies and consider enabling more policies from the [secure foundations category of Conditional Access templates](../identity/conditional-access/concept-conditional-access-policy-common?tabs=secure-foundation#template-categories). Organizations with Microsoft Entra ID P2 licenses that include Microsoft Entra ID Protection can expand on this list to include [user and sign in risk-based policies](../id-protection/howto-identity-protection-configure-risk-policies) to further strengthen their posture.
276:Microsoft recommends that organizations have two cloud-only emergency access accounts permanently assigned the [Global Administrator](/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference#global-administrator) role. These accounts are highly privileged and aren't assigned to specific individuals. The accounts are limited to emergency or "break glass" scenarios where normal accounts can't be used or all other administrators are accidentally locked out. These accounts should be created following the [emergency access account recommendations](/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access).

To help protect organizations, we're always working to improve the security of Microsoft account services. As part of this protection, customers are periodically notified for the automatic enablement of the security defaults if they:

- Don't have any Conditional Access policies
- Don't have premium licenses
- Aren’t actively using legacy authentication clients

tests/maester/entra/Test.MT.1021.ps1
    [MaesterTest(
        Id = 'MT.1021',
        Title = 'Security Defaults are enabled.',
        Product = 'entra',
        Feature = 'user-settings',
        Area = 'authentication',
        ResourceType = 'Tenant',
        Severity = 'High',
        UserImpact = 'Medium',
        ImplementationCost = 'Low',
        Mitre = ('T1078.004', 'T1110'),
        Control = ('nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(1)', 'nist-800-53-r5:IA-2(2)'),
        Service = 'Graph',
        Author = 'f-bader',
        Contributor = 'weyCC81'
    )]
    [CmdletBinding()]
    [OutputType([bool])]
    param()

    $EntraIDPlan = Get-MtLicenseInformation -Product EntraID
    if ($EntraIDPlan -ne 'Free') {
        Add-MtTestResultDetail -SkippedBecause LicensedEntraIDPremium
        return $null
    }

    $SecurityDefaults = Invoke-MtGraphRequest -RelativeUri 'policies/identitySecurityDefaultsEnforcementPolicy' -ApiVersion beta | Select-Object -ExpandProperty isEnabled

    if ($SecurityDefaults -eq $true) {
        $testResultMarkdown = "Well done. SecurityDefaults are On `n`n"
    } else {
        $testResultMarkdown = "SecurityDefaults are Off '$($SecurityDefaults)' `n`n"
    }
    $testDetailsMarkdown = 'You should enable SecurityDefaults or configure Conditional Access.'
    Add-MtTestResultDetail -Description $testDetailsMarkdown -Result $testResultMarkdown

    return ($SecurityDefaults -eq $true)
}
